01

The flat-torus trick

A square becomes periodic without bending or pinching.

Φ(u, v) = (rₓ cos 2πu, rₓ sin 2πu, rᵧ cos 2πv, rᵧ sin 2πv)

Opposite edges share the same 4D coordinates. The radii rₓ:rᵧ match the output width:height, keeping features equally sized in horizontal and vertical pixels instead of stretching non-square tiles. Unlike a doughnut embedded in 3D, this flat torus has no intrinsic distortion.

02

Activator–inhibitor chemistry

Gray–Scott reaction–diffusion evolving on the flat torus.

∂A/∂t = Dₐ∇²A − AB² + f(1 − A) ∂B/∂t = Dᵦ∇²B + AB² − (k + f)B

A feeds the system while B consumes A and inhibits nearby growth. Their different diffusion rates destabilize a uniform mixture into spots, stripes, and coral-like forms. The simulation wraps every neighbor lookup across opposite edges, so the chemistry evolves directly on a periodic 2D flat torus and remains seamless.
